model.strength: low-frequency parasitic capacitance spectral norm divided by target G spectral norm

decision.robustConditionalTarget: keep every unresolved rank-one parasitic low-frequency capacitance norm below 0.00001 of the target G norm until its coupling orientation is measured
decision.reason: at 10 ppm all 4000 draws across both pole locations pass and the 95 percent Wilson lower yield is 99.808 percent; at 30 ppm the nearer-pole lower yield falls to 98.46 percent
decision.dominantGate: inverse-metric agreement, not dispersion or loss
decision.warning: at 100 ppm the dispersion and loss p95 values remain far below their gates while inverse-metric yields fall to 60.65 and 71.4 percent
decision.measurementConsequence: the full inverse-metric gate in Wave 7.177 must not be replaced by a frequency-flatness or low-loss check
decision.supersededBy: leech-adversarial-psd-parasitic-bound-v1 lowers the joint-packet design target to 8 ppm for arbitrary PSD alignment

epistemicStatus.theorem: the added series-RLC branch is passive for positive C, L and R and the simulated static capacitance update is positive semidefinite below resonance
epistemicStatus.conditionalInference: the 10-ppm target is robust only across the two declared pole locations, Q=30 and random Rademacher coupling directions
epistemicStatus.notEstablished: one rank-one pole spans multiple parasitic modes, adversarial soft-mode alignment, distributed loss or arbitrary frequency-dependent admittance

established: a weak frequency-flat parasitic can evade dispersion and loss diagnostics while failing the inverse Leech metric; 10 ppm is the largest sampled cross-pole strength with a greater-than-99-percent Wilson lower pass yield
boundary: This is a one-pole orientation ensemble, not a device-independent tolerance theorem. Multiple coherent parasitics or alignment with the soft eigenvector can be worse and require direct measured-mode reconstruction.
